mathematical_checks: Original normal arrays and global edge counts are used throughout. The six-edge kernel is the line(1,1,1,1,-1,-1,-1); nonnegative one-quad supports in TWO arrays exclude either nonzero sign of its coefficient. Thus the two-array averaging and injectivity applications are valid, without a mistaken many-output averaging argument.

The nonvertex-to-two-copy argument first constructs an arbitrary integer-multiple decomposition by rational nullspace perturbation. Minimal multiple and minimum intersections allow absorption of all but one component. Only after connectedness is proved does Euler characteristic force n=2 and the two alternatives. No arbitrary Hilbert-basis point is presumed to have a two-copy relation.

Annular cap replacements are genuine embedded proper disks with unchanged essential boundary. Both replacements are retained, normalized separately and compared componentwise. Total least weight then kills every deficit, giving equal original edge counts without filling a sphere or asserting cap isotopy.

An actual exchange inside a marked normal product lies in one prism per local rectangle and has the required matching end/face arcs. Face-strip order and proper-disk cutting extend the prescribed maps over the prism arrangement. This proves verticality only under actual containment.

The closed even-edge surface parity proof uses a finite PL homotopy to original edge loops and mod2 preimage curves on a homotopy annulus. A nonseparating surface would give a loop crossing once. It requires neither ambient orientability nor an irreducible manifold.

The sphere capped by a between-copy annulus has even counts and separates. If the annulus lies outside the normal product, nonadjacent germs connect opposite local sphere sides through the product interior, contradicting parity. If inside, the actual vertical-product proof supplies adjacency. The proof keeps the capped sphere as a subset and never discards it or fills it by a ball.

In the sphere-annulus branch, a minimum positive disk patch has a unique opposite minimum leaf and a zero-edge annular corridor. Nested opposite caps would give two minimum leaves; circular caps cannot cover a resolved disk boundary. Reciprocal cap swaps remain embedded sphere/annulus families and remain nonproportional to primitive d, so the stated minimization applies.

Nonempty annular corridor cycles use the original diagonal continuations, not irregular switches. Every selected frontier is paired once, and every unselected regular trace is internal to the retained/discarded partition. Their union is consequently WHOLE parametrizing normalization components, not merely a locally drawn closed patch set; a nonempty zero-edge component contradicts genuine normal tetrahedral pieces.

The two-disk closed-exchange reduction also excludes proper arcs entering a circular cap. In the reciprocal-circle case both swapped disk boundaries stay their original boundaries. At least one is nullhomotopic, so that new connected disk cannot have vector jd; the vector-sum relation excludes proportionality for the other disk too. This preserves eligibility without assuming irreducibility.

For a between-copy proper exchange, the two original diagonal outputs are embedded normal disks. If both irregular outputs were essential, the actual first-return face arc strictly improves one and normalizes the other nonincreasingly, contradicting the JOINT2w bound. Actual boundary-rectangle connector paths then show that a null irregular loop forces both diagonals essential. Hence least weight/lex gives both vector d and equal adjacent/complementary cap counts.

Global proper arcs cut the original and resolved disks into genuine patch trees. A minimum boundary leaf is positive. Its opposite cap has one minimum leaf and a zero-edge rectangle; a reciprocal leaf swap preserves EACH original edge-count vector, and admissible injectivity preserves EACH original normal vector. Remaining old crossings still join different embedded families, and later partial resolutions are inherited, so reduced-pair eligibility is preserved.

When w(D)>2m, nesting/covering of opposite caps are both excluded. Repeated use of one exchange arc is excluded by the complementary-cap weight w(D)-m>m or the reciprocal-swap case. The finite leaf cycle therefore has disjoint nonempty corridors and distinct selected arcs, and the original ray pairings close a union of WHOLE normalization components, including its proper boundary in boundaryM.

When w(D)=2m, the four positive leaves exhaust the total weight and every other patch has zero edge counts. Both original and resolved dual trees are paths with two leaves. No-between-copy exchanges would preserve component labels and force both original vectors d. Any same-copy exchange equates both end-leaf counts and a between-copy exchange propagates that equality, again forcing d.

In the remaining all-between-copy covering case, adjacent cap counts at one exchange label the two resolved paths by types a,b. If a differs from b, every exchange must pair adjacent a-sides and adjacent b-sides. Restoring original diagonals therefore pairs outgoing to incoming frontier germs and gives directions on the ORIGINAL patch paths. Every original disk contains exactly one a leaf and one b leaf, so its counts are a+b=N(D), and admissible injectivity contradicts nonproportionality. This uses finite graph directions, not ambient orientation.

Fundamentalness gives coordinate gcd1; nonvertex decompositions use the FULL matching cone but remain in the original quad support. Normal replacement and finitely many natural-number coordinate minima yield the primitive extreme-ray disk in the SAME original T. The original Haken/JT two-row donors instantiate exactly these interfaces and preserve their full original Statements.
